scope: Receiver route stamina funding and recovery sprint accounting

evidenceTypes.live: Unmodified 5.1.17 failure observations; no 5.1.18 match outcome claimed here.
evidenceTypes.offline: Final canonical 5.1.18 policy/controller regressions and private native-math route replay.

liveStartBudget.causeOfNativeStaminaChange: Unknown. Reviewed client scripts read stamina; explicit no-release uses the same nil payload. No verified hidden 25-point release rule is inferred.

incidents.analysis: Native Jammed notice and speed 9 added travel delay before throw.
Avoidance denied recovery sprint while allocation accounting exhausted the cap; brief postthrow reachable forecasts were lost.
Repeated avoidance denied recovery sprint; cap reached 0.6 while native speed remained 20 and observed stamina refilled to 100.

fixes: Plan with min(current stamina, 75% of configured maximum, earliest lower Live start observed in this match). The 25% allowance is empirical and conservative, not an asserted server cost.
Clear observed start on lobby, opponent change or mode change; ignore test, invalid and late samples. Refill does not raise this match minimum; no cross-session learning or persistence.

Forecast refill of both the initial deficit and spent opening sprint, capped by actual configured maximum, rate and delayed walking interval. Opening sprint still requires current funding before future recovery.

Charge recovery cap only for observed native SprintOn at above-normal WalkSpeed during an allocated recovery interval. Denied or merely allocated requests are not charged; physical blockage does not exempt native sprint spending.

Bound each confirmed accounting interval to 100ms, intersect its end with the allocation and scheduled sprint start, and retain the 600ms confirmed-time cap. This counter is sampled confirmed time, not a claim to know exact native stamina cost.

nativeMathReplay.privacy: Authorized native Config and RouteMath were read locally and are not published. Only scalar outputs are retained.
nativeMathReplay.finding: Old 100 route suppresses opening sprint at actual 75. Reducing only the old planning budget yields an unverified best-effort route. Final 75-budget policy instead produces a funded Floater forecast and immediately requests native 27 sprint. This is a mathematical feasibility change, not proof of a live catch.

coveredCases: denied allocation does not spend cap
pending DB movement checked at 20 and 27 with 4.25 clearance

limitations: No alternate live trajectories were executed by the replay. Opponent changes, jam outcomes, physics, latency and native catch decisions remain live-test requirements.
The early Live budget observation may include a small amount of movement cost; conservative downward-only handling deliberately avoids optimistic refill evidence.
A hard jam can still make a fixed already-submitted route unreachable; this update does not remove native jam or catch validation.
No wins, guaranteed catches, training improvement or server acceptance are claimed.
